chunks: Al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Yunus ibn Bahman, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): A Christian relative of mine sent me as a gift some roasted chickens and chicks, and prepared for me a 'faludhajah' (a type of dish). Should I eat it? He said: 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.فَالُوذَجَةَ: a type of dish (likely a stew or mixed dish)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat roasted chicken gifted by a Christian?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) permits consuming roasted poultry gifted by a Christian relative, affirming the general permissibility of the food of the People of the Book. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that such food is not inherently impure (*najis*) nor prohibited, provided it is not specifically slaughtered in the name of other than God, thereby facilitating social interaction and gift-giving (*mu'atara*) with non-Muslims.
